text:
olivia: Quick sync — we need to size a Dedicated EU pool for the new 70B q4f16 bring-up. Goal: 99th token latency budget for typical chat flows <= 250ms, steady-state 200 reqs/s across region with 2x burst runway. suggestions on gpu count / per-GPU concurrency / kernel split?

miguel: +1. did perf runs yesterday. baseline numbers attached in the perf sheet (link: https://redwood.internal/perf/eu-70b-q4f16). short summary: H100 gives ~2.4x tokens/s vs A100 for this quant config, p95 token latency on H100 is ~22ms (seq=512), A100 p95 ~55ms. throughput numbers are for continuous generation (no external I/O).

linh: thanks — can you paste the command you used for the harness? want to reproduce locally.

miguel: sure — small snippet:
```
./bench.sh --model redwood/70b-q4f16 --seq 512 --batch 1 --decode greedy --kernels auto --iters 1000 
```
perf-bot: summary posted: avg_tokens_per_sec: H100=780, A100=320; p50_token_ms: H100=8.6, A100=21.7; p95_token_ms: H100=21.9, A100=54.8. (runs: eu-west1-h100, eu-west1-a100)

sam: ok that's helpful. If we assume average response length 60 tokens, that implies per-request generation time (token pipeline) ~60 * p95_token_ms. For H100 at p95 that's ~1.3s worst-case per request, A100 ~3.3s — but we can parallelize by concurrency.

olivia: target 200 rps steady-state. using H100 numbers: effective rps per GPU = tokens_per_sec / avg_tokens_per_request = 780 / 60 = 13 rps. so need ~16 GPUs to hit 200 rps. that's without burst runway or headroom. with 2x burst runway and ~60% target util we probably want 16 * 2 / 0.6 = ~54 GPUs — that seems high. are we double-counting?

miguel: two caveats — bench numbers assume continuous streaming of tokens from a single session; real traffic is many short sessions which improve batching efficiency but also increase overhead. also prefix caching will cut work on many requests. i prefer modeling with observed request size distribution: median 20 tokens, tail 180. with that the effective avg tokens/request is ~35 in production. re-calc: 780/35 = 22 rps per H100 -> 200/22 ~= 10 GPUs. with 2x burst runway and 70% target util => (10 * 2) / 0.7 = ~29 GPUs. that's more reasonable.

linh: can we mix GPU types to save $ while keeping latency SLO? e.g., primary H100 pool for low-latency routes and A100 cold pool for non-critical or heavy-batch workloads. routing policy could send 80% priority traffic to H100 then fallback to A100.

sam: yes. propose: base H100 committed pool = 12 GPUs (handles steady-state + small headroom), autoscale up to 28 H100 on surge; A100 spare pool = 10 GPUs for cheapest spill; routing policy: route by route_priority + max_latency SLO.

olivia: what about kernel selection/quant variants? can we reduce H100 count by using a different kernel or quant mode?

miguel: we ran a kernel sweep: for 70B q4f16, aten kernels gave worse perf. fused-attention + custom kernels gave best perf on H100. also q8_0 (8-bit) brings 15-25% tokens/s uplift but introduces quality delta for some eval prompts. need eval suite pass before switching.

perf-bot: kernel sweep results (summary): custom-fused (H100) + q4f16 -> baseline; q8_0 -> +18% tokens/s, small eval regressions on instruction-following set (5% drop on targeted prompts).

linh: ops ask: what autoscale policy numbers? we need cooldowns, instance startup times. H100 warmup ~180s from cold start with container startup + model load; preloaded cache option reduces cold-to-ready to ~30s if we keep standby kernels loaded.

sam: propose autoscale rules: scale up aggressively (policy: target_util 65%, scale_step 4 GPUs), scale down conservatively (cooldown 10m). maintain 4 preloaded standby GPUs to absorb fast bursts.

olivia: runnable plan suggestion:
- commit 12 H100 for EU dedicated pool (reserved)
- add autoscale cap to 28 H100
- provision 10 A100 as secondary pool with cheaper pricing tier
- set routing: default -> H100; overflow -> A100; fallbacks for region failover to us-west with same model variant
- autoscale policy as sam suggested + 4 preloaded standby H100 (preload flag)
- run eval suite overnight with q8_0 variant to measure regressions; if <2% degradation, enable q8_0 on H100 only and re-run capacity calc

miguel: I can run an overnight sim with real request traces (we have 72h logs) and output projected pool utilizations. I expect committed 12 + autoscale to 28 will hit p95 latency SLO for 95% of trial windows. will post sim outputs tomorrow morning.

linh: ops question: what's the estimated monthly cost delta for 12 committed H100 vs 12 A100? finance asked.

miguel: rough — H100 reserved ~1.8x A100 reserved for our vendor pricing. I'll add a short cost table in the sim gist.

olivia: ok thanks. next steps: miguel run sim + attach charts, linch run eval with q8_0 overnight, sam prepare autoscale config PR with the preload flag and routing rules. we'll sync tomorrow 10:30. :thumbsup:
